DOCX paragraph verification: When checking a DOCX for required lines and no extras, compare the extracted non-empty paragraph list to the full expected sequence; checking only for absence of unexpected lines can falsely pass empty or subset documents.
DOCX exact line verification: When verifying an exact DOCX structure, parse word/document.xml and compare extracted paragraph text, but also enforce exact counts of expected paragraphs to prevent duplicate expected lines from passing as no-extra-content.
DOCX navigation-list verification: When verifying list-style content in DOCX, parse paragraph text and preferably require exact item paragraphs or bullet/numbered list entries, not only substring presence, to avoid false positives from overlapping terms such as 游戏, QQ游戏, and 游戏中心.
DOCX table structure verification: For DOCX summary tasks, python-docx checks should enforce table row count, column count, exact row order, exact cell text, and paragraph/table ordering; searching for substrings anywhere in the document allows many false positives.
DOCX table verification: For generated DOCX summaries, parse the document with python-docx and enforce exact table count, exact row count, row order, header labels, and cell values rather than accepting unordered rows or substring matches that can pass extra or malformed content.
DOCX task initial-state resistance: For document-edit tasks, do not award standalone partial credit for pre-existing source content such as the original bullet count; require the newly added target section/content before giving any positive score, otherwise the initial document can receive nonzero reward.
DOCX end-of-document insertion verificat: For DOCX tasks, use python-docx on the local cached path returned by vm_file and check paragraph order, exact text, and relevant styles/numbering XML rather than relying on file existence or visual inspection.
source dependency verification: A rule that only re-reads the immutable source file can pass in the initial state and should not contribute reward unless it is used to derive expected values that are then checked against user-created outputs.
DOCX content verification: When a Writer document has a specified title and lines, parse the DOCX structure and verify the expected paragraph order rather than only checking that the strings occur somewhere.
plain text exact line verification: For instructions requiring exactly one line in a plain-text file, compare the full file content allowing at most a single trailing newline rather than filtering non-empty lines or stripping whitespace.
initial-state false positives: A rule that only validates sampled source files or expected data, without checking a user-created artifact, can produce positive initial reward and should be removed or converted into an expected_getter used by an artifact-checking rule.
